name: Sweden
currency_note: Sweden uses kronor (SEK); the app shows euros. Tax figures below are in kronor.

tax_year.return_due: File the return in spring of the next year; for income year 2025 the last day was 4 May 2026, and Skatteverket publishes the date for 2027 in advance.

summary: Investment income (capital income, inkomst av kapital) is taxed at a flat 30%. On an ordinary account you pay 30% on gains, dividends and interest. On an investment savings account (ISK) or a capital insurance (kapitalförsäkring) you instead pay a small yearly tax on the account value, and from 2026 the first SEK 300,000 of these savings together is tax-free.

topics.title: Profit when you sell
points: Outside an ISK or kapitalförsäkring, a gain on shares, funds and bonds is capital income taxed at 30%.
The gain is the sale price after fees minus the cost (omkostnadsbelopp). The cost is worked out with the average method (genomsnittsmetoden) across all your purchases of the same share.
For listed shares and listed funds you may instead use the standard method (schablonmetoden): the cost is set at 20% of the sale price after fees, so 80% of the price counts as gain.
Sales of listed shares are reported on form K4 (bilaga K4) with your return.

topics.title: Dividends
points: Dividends on shares and fund units held outside an ISK or kapitalförsäkring are taxed at 30%.
Banks and brokers report dividends to Skatteverket, and the amount is pre-filled in your return.

topics.title: Interest on savings
points: Interest is taxed at 30%.
A Swedish bank reports the interest to Skatteverket and normally withholds tax on it during the year.

Cash inside an ISK is covered by the yearly standard tax. Only if the account pays more than the government borrowing rate plus 1 point (or 1.25%, whichever is higher) at some point in the year is that interest taxed separately (rule from 2025).

topics.title: Funds and ETFs
points: If you own fund units (fondandelar) outside an ISK or kapitalförsäkring, you are taxed each year on a standard income (schablonintäkt) of 0.4% of their value on 1 January, whether you sold or not. At 30% this is a tax of 0.12% of the value.
Your bank or fund company calculates the standard income and reports it, together with fund dividends and sales.
When you sell, the gain or loss is taxed as for shares, at 30%.

topics.title: Tax-free amounts
points: From 2026, the first SEK 300,000 of your combined savings in ISK, kapitalförsäkring and PEPP products is tax-free (skattefri grundnivå). In 2025 it was SEK 150,000.
You get this as an automatic deduction in your return; you do not need to ask for it. The deduction is used against ISK first.
For 2026 the deduction is at most SEK 10,650 (SEK 300,000 × 3.55%).

topics.title: Tax-free and tax-deferred accounts
points: Investment savings account (investeringssparkonto, ISK): gains, dividends and losses inside it are not taxed or declared. Instead you pay tax on a standard income (schablonintäkt) worked out from the account value.

For 2026 the standard income is 3.55% of the capital base: the government borrowing rate on 30 November 2025 (2.55%) plus 1 point, and never below 1.25%. Taxed at 30%, this is 1.065% of the capital base above the tax-free level.
The capital base is the account value at the start of each quarter plus all deposits in the year, divided by four. There is no deposit limit.
Moving shares from an ordinary account into an ISK counts as a sale, so any gain is taxed at that point.

Capital insurance (kapitalförsäkring): with a Swedish policy the insurer pays a yearly yield tax (avkastningsskatt) and charges it to you, and you declare nothing. With a foreign policy you declare it yourself: the base is the capital times the borrowing rate plus 1 point (at least 1.25%), and the tax is 30% of that base.
The rate for 2027 depends on the borrowing rate on 30 November 2026, which was not yet known when this page was checked.

topics.title: Losses
points: A loss on listed shares or listed share funds can be set in full against gains on listed shares and share funds in the same year.
What is left of the loss after that counts at 70% (kvotering) against your other capital income.
If your capital income is negative overall (underskott av kapital), you get a reduction of your other tax: 30% of the deficit up to SEK 100,000 and 21% of the part above.
Skatteverket does the netting itself when it calculates your tax. Gains and losses inside an ISK are not declared at all.

topics.title: Foreign shares
points: Foreign tax withheld on dividends can be credited against Swedish tax. Skatteverket does this automatically when the foreign tax appears in a report (kontrolluppgift) from your bank.
The credit is usually limited to 15% of the dividend (10% for Austria and 5% for the United Kingdom). Tax withheld above that must be reclaimed from the other country.
Foreign tax on dividends inside an ISK can also be credited; the income it is set against may not exceed the ISK standard income.
If the foreign tax was not reported, you can ask for the credit in your return or on form SKV 2703.

topics.title: What your broker does and what you do
points: Swedish banks and brokers normally report your sales, dividends, interest and fund standard income to Skatteverket, and the figures are pre-filled in your return.
For an ISK the bank reports only the standard income; gains and losses inside the account are not declared.
If a sale was not reported, or you want to correct it, you enter it yourself on form K4 (listed shares in section A).
Skatteverket's e-service can calculate the cost with the standard method and fill in K4 for you.

topics.title: Crypto
points: A gain on selling or exchanging crypto, or paying with it, is taxed at 30%. A loss is deductible at 70%.
The cost must be worked out with the average method across all your purchases of the same coin, on all exchanges and wallets. The 20% standard method may not be used for crypto.
Crypto sales go on form K4, section D.

dates.what: Fund units are valued on this day for the yearly fund standard income.
Last day to file the 2025 return in 2026; the 2027 date is set by Skatteverket.
The government borrowing rate on this day sets next year's ISK and kapitalförsäkring rate.

upcoming: Sweden had no new government after the September 2026 election when this page was checked. The 2027 budget handed to parliament on 12 November 2026 is a caretaker budget meant to contain no new policy, so tax changes for 2027 may follow once a government is formed.
not_covered: Unlisted shares and closely held companies (fåmansföretag, K10 and K12 rules).
Pensions and pension savings other than the shared tax-free level.
Moving to or from Sweden, and people taxed in Sweden for only part of the year.
